what: A replay of one Design Studio run: Can we design a fruit fly that lives longer?
live_hint: studio-live.html polls POST /tool/session_read on a running sim-engine/http.mjs and shows that instead when it answers. Start one with: node sim-engine/http.mjs
question: Can we design a fruit fly that lives longer?
verdict: The question has an answer now, and it is a sharp one: doubling the intrinsic lifespan gives 2.00x in a vial and 1.09x in the wild, because the ceiling set by extrinsic mortality is 12.5 days whatever happens inside the animal. That is the Medawar-Williams argument arriving as arithmetic over three declared rates, and it is the first result in these runs that needed two layers at once: the ecology layer names what is eating the fly, and the performance layer says what that costs the design.

entries.body: generation 0: Put the request through the front door first. The interesting part is not what the parser makes of "fruit fly" -- it is what it makes of "lives longer", which is the entire request.

entries.author: agent:long-lived-fly
entries.body: the organism is named (fruit fly) and placed as Drosophila melanogaster, and the REQUIREMENT is not read at all: 0 criteria. "Lives longer" is not in the spec vocabulary, so the clause stays unparsed. That is correct behaviour and it is the whole finding: there is no scenario, no metric and no threshold anywhere in this engine for how long an organism lives.

unparsed.of_clause: I want a fruit fly that lives longer
unparsed.reason: organism "fruit fly" has no reference parameter set in this engine (it holds measured parameters for: zebrafish, flying fish, winged zebrafish, wingless flying fish, TFF, the ff-zf chimera). It is not mapped to a "close" one, because the nearest fish is not this animal. A taxon-based design can still be built from it: see spec.taxon, organism_create {taxon} and organism_from_blueprint. The rest of this clause IS parsed: any criterion in it is on the spec, and will be judged once a parameter set for this clade exists.

detail.a_bug_this_run_found: Before this run the same sentence produced a GLIDE criterion. familyGlide matches the free-standing word "fly", `fruit fly` contains one, and the parser read the name of the animal as a requirement that it be able to fly -- a criterion nobody asked for, attached to a request about lifespan. Two-word insect names ending in "fly" are now organism names and are taken out of the clause before the criterion families read it.

entries.author: agent:long-lived-fly
entries.body: the front door now ROUTES the requirement instead of dropping it: 0 requirement(s) for physics_check, 1 for performance_check, 0 that no layer takes. "lives longer" goes to performance_check { kind: "lifespan" }, and the quantities that check needs are the designer's to declare. Before this the whole clause came back unparsed, which read as a parse failure when it was a capability gap -- two different things the routing block now tells apart.

entries.author: agent:long-lived-fly
entries.body: 12 scenario modules exist and 0 of them measure anything like a lifespan: none. The scenarios are glide, current, temperature, depth, altitude, predator, grip and the rest -- every one of them a question asked of an organism at an age, not a question about how many ages it gets. The engine has growth tracks (ontogeny.json, for two teleosts) and no senescence model for anything. There is no mortality rate, no survival curve and no cause of death in this repository.

detail.searched_for: lifespan, senescence, longevity, mortality, ageing -- across sim-engine/ and the Lean law set

entries.author: agent:long-lived-fly
entries.body: generation 1: Build the organism anyway. A gap is easier to argue with when the thing beside it is real: the anatomy layer has a great deal to say about Drosophila melanogaster and none of it bears on how long the animal lives.

entries.author: agent:long-lived-fly
entries.body: Drosophila melanogaster resolves and the hierarchy is substantial: 5 organ systems, 26 organs, 24 tissues, 45 cell types, all Uberon and Cell Ontology terms with the query that produced each one. Every term is a structure. Not one of them is a rate, and lifespan is a rate.

entries.author: agent:long-lived-fly
entries.body: a STATE resolves at each of the four declared stages, and the track is NOT MONOTONIC: egg 1e-8 kg / 0.0005 m, larva 0.0000015 kg / 0.0045 m, pupa 0.0000012 kg / 0.003 m, adult 0.000001 kg / 0.0025 m. The larva is heavier and longer than the adult it becomes, so a growth curve for this animal goes up and then down. Every value carries kind "assumed (declared by the design)" -- declared, not measured -- and nothing here simulates the transition between any two of them.

detail.what_it_is_not: Four declared masses at four declared ages. No cell divides, no imaginal disc forms, and the only Lean law about time (genotype-developmental-ordering) certifies that a declared ordering is acyclic -- it does not supply one.

entries.author: agent:long-lived-fly
entries.body: 17 cannot-evaluate, 18 out-of-scope. No law in the set bears on lifespan for any clade, so even a law base written about insects would not have answered this.

entries.author: agent:long-lived-fly
entries.body: generation 2: The fly walks and flies. Ask the locomotion layer both, partly to exercise it on an insect and partly because both flight branches should refuse, for two different reasons worth telling apart: powered flight is a power question this layer cannot take, and the area question underneath it runs into a coefficient policy that records Insecta as inapplicable rather than unmeasured.

entries.author: agent:long-lived-fly
entries.body: nothing this layer can check contradicts the design. That is NOT a finding that it moves: there is no muscle here, no metabolism, no control and no energy budget, and 2 of the 4 checks are regime indicators that never fail anything.

detail.froude: Equal Froude number is a NECESSARY condition for two animals to move in a dynamically similar way, and later work is explicit that it is not sufficient -- cursorial and non-cursorial mammals do not move similarly at equal Fr. The widely quoted walk-to-run transition at Fr = 0.5 is a human result. Turning any of that into a pass or a fail for an arbitrary clade would be borrowing a threshold across exactly the gap this repository keeps finding and removing, so this check reports the number and stops.

entries.author: agent:long-lived-fly
entries.body: PARTLY EVALUATED: 1 of the 2 checks could not be run at all -- lift_carries_the_weight (the question asked is about POWERED flight, and this check cannot answer it. It compares lift with weight at a given airspeed, which is an area question; powered flight is a power question -- whether the flight muscle can supply the induced and profile power through a wingbeat, continuously, at that animal's mass. That needs a coefficient measured through a wingbeat and a muscle power density for the clade, and this repository has neither.). The checks that did run found no contradiction, and a check that did not run is not a check that passed. The refusal is about POWERED flight, which is the deeper of the two reasons this could not be answered: an area inequality is not a power budget.

lift.limiting_factor: the question asked is about POWERED flight, and this check cannot answer it. It compares lift with weight at a given airspeed, which is an area question; powered flight is a power question -- whether the flight muscle can supply the induced and profile power through a wingbeat, continuously, at that animal's mass. That needs a coefficient measured through a wingbeat and a muscle power density for the clade, and this repository has neither.

entries.author: agent:long-lived-fly
entries.body: asked a pure area question about an insect, the coefficient policy refuses -- and refuses for a reason that is NOT "nobody measured one": a steady maximum lift coefficient is the WRONG QUANTITY for Drosophila melanogaster, which the NCBI taxonomy places inside Insecta. This is a decision, not a missing measurement: NOT a missing measurement. Dickinson, Lehmann and Sane measured for

detail.reason: a steady maximum lift coefficient is the WRONG QUANTITY for Drosophila melanogaster, which the NCBI taxonomy places inside Insecta. This is a decision, not a missing measurement: NOT a missing measurement. A steady maximum lift coefficient is the wrong quantity for a flapping insect wing, and adding one would answer the question with a model its own source says does not apply. Dickinson, Lehmann and Sane measured forces on a dynamically scaled robotic Drosophila melanogaster wing and reported that the enhanced aerodynamic performance of insects comes from three interacting mechanisms -- delayed stall during the translational phase, and rotational circulation and wake capture during stroke reversals. The second and third exist only because the wing rotates and reverses, and a steady coefficient represents neither. Using one here would compute a lift that omits a large part of where an insect's lift actually comes from, and present the shortfall as a property of the animal. A right answer needs a quasi-steady model with translational, rotational and added-mass terms, and the wing kinematics to drive it; or a measured force trace through the wingbeat, which is what the robotic-wing experiments produce; either way a stroke amplitude, a wingbeat frequency and an angle-of-attack schedule, none of which this repository holds for any insect. Source: Dickinson MH, Lehmann FO, Sane SP 1999, Wing rotation and the aerodynamic basis of insect flight, Science 284(5422):1954-1960 (doi 10.1126/science.284.5422.1954).
detail.why_this_matters: Dickinson, Lehmann and Sane showed on a dynamically scaled robotic Drosophila wing that an insect gets a large part of its lift from rotational circulation and wake capture, which exist only because the wing reverses. A steady maximum lift coefficient represents neither. Borrowing the flying fish or the sugar glider would have produced a number; adding an insect number would have produced a number too, and both would be answering with a model the source says does not apply. The table therefore records Insecta as INAPPLICABLE with what a right check would need, which is a different claim from a missing measurement and sends a caller somewhere different.

entries.author: agent:long-lived-fly
entries.body: generation 3: Ecology is the one layer with any purchase here, and only sideways: a longer-lived fly is a fly exposed to predation for longer. The databases cannot tell us the lifespan, but they can tell us what is on record as eating this animal and whether any of it is in the place we are asking about.

entries.author: agent:long-lived-fly
entries.body: GBIF holds 4,503 occurrence records for Drosophila melanogaster Meigen, 1830, concentrated in KR, US, SE. In Greater Boston GBIF holds 58,684 records; the 10 most-recorded non-Aves species are listed. None of the 29 taxa GloBI records as eating Drosophila melanogaster Meigen, 1830 appear in this box's top 10 by record count. Read that as a gap in two databases before reading it as an empty niche: the box list is truncated, record-ranked and missing every Aves species. No population parameters were declared, so whether this design could establish against what is there has NOT been evaluated. That question needs numbers no occurrence database contains.

detail.recorded_range: GBIF holds 4,503 occurrence records for Drosophila melanogaster Meigen, 1830, concentrated in KR, US, SE.
detail.relationships_note: Grouped from GloBI's own interaction types. 28 taxa recorded eating this clade, 14 recorded parasitising it, 3 in a recorded mutualistic or symbiotic relationship with it, 13 it is recorded hosting. COMPETITION IS NOT AMONG THEM, and that is not an oversight: competition is the one ecological relationship that leaves almost no direct observational trace, because it is two organisms NOT doing something to each other. GloBI records interactions that somebody watched happen. Nobody watches an exclusion. Types this grouping does not recognise, left in "other": hasParasitoid.
detail.predation_pressure: None of the 29 taxa GloBI records as eating Drosophila melanogaster Meigen, 1830 appear in this box's top 10 by record count. Read that as a gap in two databases before reading it as an empty niche: the box list is truncated, record-ranked and missing every Aves species.
detail.the_sideways_point: GloBI records real predators of this clade with studies behind them. What it cannot give is a predation RATE, and a lifespan question needs a rate: an organism that lives twice as long in a jar may live no longer at all in a place where something eats it every week. The layer supplies the list and refuses the rate.

entries.author: agent:long-lived-fly
entries.body: generation 4: The lifespan layer exists now. It needs three rates: what kills the fly from the inside, what the design proposes to change that to, and what kills it from the outside. The third is the one the ecology layer bears on -- 29 taxa are on record eating this clade -- and turning a predator list into a hazard is a judgement somebody has to make and state, so the run states it.

entries.author: agent:long-lived-fly
entries.body: The design changes the INTRINSIC hazard by a factor of 0.5 -- a 2x longer intrinsic lifespan. With the extrinsic hazard at 0.08 /day, expected lifetime goes from 10.345-10.345 days to 11.321-11.321 days: a factor of 1.094 to 1.094. Extrinsic mortality dominates. Abolishing intrinsic mortality ENTIRELY would give 12.5 days, only 1.208x the baseline, so no change to the intrinsic term can buy much here: the animal is not dying of being old.

detail.model: Constant two-term hazard, E[T] = 1/(h_intrinsic + h_extrinsic). Exact arithmetic over the declared rates.
detail.model_caveat: A CONSTANT hazard makes the lifetime exponential, and real survival curves are not: hazards rise with age, which is what senescence IS, and a Gompertz or Weibull form would capture that. Fitting one needs survival data this repository holds for no organism. So the shape here is assumed, not fitted, and the expectation is a first-order statement that is most wrong exactly where senescence matters most -- at the old end of the curve.
cannot_say: HOW the design would live longer: no pathway, no gene, no mechanism is represented anywhere in this repository
whether the intrinsic hazard the design claims is achievable at all
what the change costs: life-history theory expects a longer-lived design to pay in fecundity or growth, and nothing here prices that
whether the extrinsic hazard stays put: an organism that lives longer is exposed longer, and may be exposed differently

entries.author: agent:long-lived-fly
entries.body: The design changes the INTRINSIC hazard by a factor of 0.5 -- a 2x longer intrinsic lifespan. With the extrinsic hazard at 0.000001 /day, expected lifetime goes from 59.996-59.996 days to 119.986-119.986 days: a factor of 2 to 2. There is headroom: with intrinsic mortality abolished entirely the expectation would be 1.00e+6 days, 1.67e+4x the baseline, so the intrinsic term is worth working on in this environment. THIS IS THE POINT OF THE PAIR: the same design, the same intrinsic change, and the answer is 2.00x in a vial against 1.09x where the animal actually lives. A longevity result is a statement about an environment as much as about an organism, and the two numbers come from the same arithmetic with one input changed.

honesty.mesh: No generation of this animal has a surface mesh. anatomy-model/parametric is a parametric TELEOST builder and Blender is not installed on the machine this ran on, so no .glb was built and none is shown. The 3D view draws the ONTOLOGY HIERARCHY -- which structures the design has and what contains what -- and that is structure without shape: it cannot be flown, measured for area, or printed.
honesty.declared: The mass, membrane area and airspeed in generations 1-3 are DESIGN INPUTS. Each carries a source string saying so. Nobody has measured a winged mouse and nothing here pretends otherwise.
honesty.verdicts: Every verdict on this page is the string the tool itself returned, with the numbers it returned, copied from the session log. Nothing is recomputed here and nothing is rounded for display except where the page shows a fixed number of decimals.
